operations.gives: Rise, set, transit and twilight in a window
The sun's azimuth and altitude from a place

fields.startUtc: The window's start, ISO 8601 with Z. Usually midnight UTC; a few cases start at a place's local midnight.
fields.windowInHours: The window's length: 24 in every case here. More than 0 and at most 48.
fields.instantUtc: An instant, ISO 8601 with Z, read as UT1
fields.riseUtc: The first moment in the window the top of the sun reaches the horizon: its centre at −0.833°, geometric. null if it doesn't happen in the window. To the second, compared within 60 s: USNO gives the minute.
fields.transitUtc: The first moment in the window the sun crosses the meridian, highest in the sky. Left out when the sun stays down all window, where USNO gives none.
fields.civilDawnUtc: Centre at −6°, rising. null if it doesn't happen in the window
fields.isAlwaysUp: true when the sun is above −0.833° for the whole window
fields.isAlwaysDown: true when it's below −0.833° for the whole window
fields.azimuthInDegrees: 0 to 360, clockwise from north. Left out near the zenith.
fields.altitudeInDegrees: −90 to 90, of the sun's centre, geometric: no refraction

cases.note: A window from local midnight across the date line.
Midnight sun: no rise or set, always up, and a transit.
Polar night with civil twilight at midday.
It never gets darker than civil twilight: nautical and astronomical dawn and dusk are null.
A UTC day: the set (evening before, local time) comes before the rise.
Polar night: always down, but nautical and astronomical twilight still come and go.
Near the south pole in December: always up.
USNO lists the sun only when it's up; below the horizon Skyfield answers.
Midnight sun, low in the north.
